fix.note: Spoken exclamation; 우와 is a stronger version.

ex.en: Wow, the view is really nice!
Wow, this is so delicious.
Wow, it's already twelve?
This summer is really hot.
Half of this year is already gone.
My daughter starts elementary school this year.

fix.note: 기대하다 = to look forward to; 기대돼요 = I'm excited.

ex.en: This hotel is better than I expected.
That restaurant was worse than I expected.
Don't get your hopes up too much.
The explanation is clear, so it's easy to understand.
I'm sure I left the keys here.
That person's answer wasn't clear.
My uncle works at a car factory.
I went on a factory tour.
This is a factory outlet store, so it's cheap.

fix.note: 그만하다 = to stop; 그만두다 = to quit.

ex.en: Stop crying now.
I'll stop eating, I'm full.
Stop playing and do your homework.
The weather is getting colder and colder.
Korean is getting more and more fun.
The child looks more and more like his dad.
Send me any fun videos you find.
I'll film a video of the baby and send it.
I followed along with a cooking video.
I got a cut on my hand.
I hope the cut heals fast.
I was hurt by what they said.

notes: Dropped 노력 (duplicate of 노력하다, examples were verb forms). Replaced examples duplicating other entries or using other lemmas (기대돼요, 분명히), unnatural 점점 재미있어요, odd 공장/그만 sentences.
